method: microspectrophotometry of single photoreceptor cells, glass eels
conditions: MSP on dark-adapted (overnight) retinae enucleated under dim red light; sample sizes per stage 9 glass eels (Hsiukuluan River mouth, eastern Taiwan), 4 cultured yellow eels (3-year-old fish from an eel farm, Pingtung County) and 2 wild yellow eels (upstream of Laomei Stream, northern Taiwan), about 40 measurements per specimen, absorbance curves template-fitted and kept only if lambda-max SD was below 7.5 nm; Results print rod means 493 +/- 4.7 nm (glass) and 489 +/- 6.1 nm (cultured yellow), 489 +/- 5.1 nm for wild yellow, with no significant difference between cultured and wild yellow eels and the glass-eel value significantly different from the other stages (t-tests, Table 2); the Results say only a single cone class was observed and only in cultured and wild yellow eels, and give no cone values or cone sample size in the text, so the 508 and 517 nm cone figures appear only in the abstract; the text does not say whether cones were found in glass eels; no silver eels were measured; the authors' abstract conclusion that the eel is colour-blind rests on this single cone class

method: frozen eyeball homogenised in 1% CHAPS buffer under dim red light (>640 nm), extract centrifuged at 50,000 g, extraction repeated until the supernatant was colourless (four extracts); absorption spectra at 28 C, hydroxylamine added to 100 mM, residual pigment bleached with orange and yellow light; absorption maximum read from the resulting difference spectrum
conditions: deep-sea snailfish taken at the Hatoma Knoll hydrothermal vent field, Okinawa Trough, 1480-1530 m, by ROV; number of fish and collection date not stated; one eyeball kept for RNA and the other frozen for protein; the absolute spectrum also showed a component near 410 nm (a hydroxylamine-labile difference peak at 414 nm the authors could not identify) alongside the 480 nm absorption they attribute to rhodopsin; the recombinant protein expressed in HEK293EBNA cells with 11-cis retinal also peaked at 480 nm; no replicate count or statistics given for the spectra; the abstract's link to blue-light sensitivity is the authors' inference, not measured

source.authors: Rie Sakata, Ryo Kabutomori, Keiko Okano, Hiromasa Mitsui, Akihiro Takemura, Tetsuya Miwa, Hiroyuki Yamamoto, Toshiyuki Okano
source.title: Rhodopsin in the Dark Hot Sea: Molecular Analysis of Rhodopsin in a Snailfish, Careproctus rhodomelas, Living near the Deep-Sea Hydrothermal Vent

quote: Proteins were solubilized from the C. rhodomelas eyeball and subjected to spectroscopic analysis, which revealed the presence of a pigment characterized by an absorption maximum (λmax) at 480 nm.
note: Family and order are from the Fig 1A caption ('Order Scorpaeniformes, Liparidae, snailfish'). Page prints the Creative Commons Attribution License; Crossref licence CC BY 4.0, content-version vor, issued 2015-08-14.

method: behavioural valvometry: valve-opening amplitude recorded by high-frequency noninvasive valvometry while 3 min pure tones (70 s fade-in, no fade-out) were played in a flume; response = drop in valve opening of at least 10% during the fade-in; logistic regression of response against sound pressure level and shell acceleration
conditions: two groups of 16 farmed diploid oysters, about 18 months old, 70-75 mm shell length, bought from farmers in Arcachon Bay, France, acclimatised at least 10 days in a 350 L running-seawater raceway at 15.0 +/- 0.5 C; group A tested April-May 2015 with 90-800 Hz tones, group B September 2015 with 10-80 Hz tones, tones given one per 30 min; frequency order and randomisation not stated; stimuli stated as waterborne sinusoidal tones 10 Hz to 20 kHz with accelerometer on the shell and hydrophone; 60-95% of animals responded at 10-200 Hz; thresholds modelled only from 10 to 400 Hz (500 and 600 Hz gave no significant model); least energy about 0.02 m/s2 (122 dBrms re 1 uPa) at 10-80 Hz; 700-1000 Hz and 8-10 kHz not tested for loudspeaker limits; a 1-20 kHz sweep at about 148 dBrms (about 0.1 m/s2) caused no reaction; the authors note a partial valve closure cannot be told from a nociceptive response and that oysters likely detect lower energies. This is a behavioural valve response, with particle motion measured at the shell and no pressure receptor involved; whether it counts as hearing is an owner ruling (see progress note)

source.title: The sense of hearing in the Pacific oyster, Magallana gigas

where: Abstract (PLOS page opened with WebFetch, sentence read twice, whole)
quote: At high enough acoustic energy, oysters transiently closed their valves in response to frequencies in the range of 10 to <1000 Hz, with maximum sensitivity from 10 to 200 Hz.
note: Value [10, 1000] is the upper bound as printed ('<1000 Hz'); best frequency band 10-200 Hz in the quote. Family and order follow main's Crassostrea virginica rows. Magallana gigas is the name used in the paper title and on main's try-species list (the older Crassostrea gigas is the synonym). Crossref licence CC BY 4.0, vor, issued 2017-10-25; page prints the Creative Commons Attribution License.

value: lowest larval AEBR thresholds 140-150 dB re 1 uPa (-33 to -23 dB re 1 g) at frequencies below 225 Hz
method: behavioural: acoustically evoked behavioural response (AEBR), a startle-like caudal-fin movement of more than 50% of total length straight after the stimulus; fish randomly presented 100 ms tones with 6 ms ramps at 75 Hz and 105-425 Hz in 40 Hz steps, level 154 down to 136 dB re 1 uPa in 3 dB steps; sound pressure measured with a hydrophone at the fish position (equal amplitude within +/-2 dB), particle acceleration calculated from it by script and checked with an accelerometer
conditions: larvae from nest rocks collected in the May-August breeding season from intertidal sites in California and Washington, reared in 190 L aquaria at about 15 C; size groups small 1.5-1.7 cm TL (n=19), medium 1.8-2.4 cm (n=19), large 2.5-2.7 cm (n=12), juveniles 2.8-3.2 cm (n=17), per-frequency n not stated; no AEBR below 1.4 cm TL and all larvae of 1.8 cm or more responded to a 154 dB broadband click; Results give best evoked frequencies of 75-145 Hz with thresholds at best frequency of 133-151 dB re 1 uPa, a wider range than the abstract's 140-150 dB; MANOVA found frequency, size group and their interaction significant; the 1.8-2.4 cm group had lower thresholds (about 4-7 dB at 75, 105 and 145 Hz) but the distribution of best frequencies did not differ among size groups (F3,57 = 2.24, p = 0.095); thresholds rose with frequency; lateral line not needed to evoke the response; laboratory-reared

source.title: Development of the Acoustically Evoked Behavioral Response in Larval Plainfin Midshipman Fish, Porichthys notatus

where: Abstract (PLOS page opened with WebFetch, sentence read twice, whole)
quote: Lowest AEBR thresholds were 140–150 dB re 1 µPa or −33 to −23 dB re 1 g for frequencies below 225 Hz.
note: Larval stage, not adult. Family from the paper's phrase 'Batrachoidid fishes, including midshipman'; order is on main's taxonomy table (Batrachoidiformes). Crossref licence CC BY 3.0, vor, issued 2013-12-10; page prints the Creative Commons Attribution License.

units: nm (peak of the ERG spectral sensitivity curve)
method: electroretinography (b-wave), dark-adapted whole-eye ERG; sensitivity from irradiance needed for a 5 microvolt criterion response
conditions: wild fish taken by daytime bottom trawl at 100-117 m in the Apostle Islands region of Lake Superior on 13 Nov 2012 and 26 June 2013 and held at the University of Minnesota Duluth (kiyi tested within 4 days of capture, siscowet within 3 weeks, sculpin within 2 months); number of fish per species and body sizes not stated; dark-adapted 30 min, anaesthetised with buffered 0.002% MS-222 and immobilised with pancuronium bromide; ERG with a silver-silver chloride electrode in the vitreous, monochromatic light 400-700 nm in 25 nm steps in random order from a 100 W tungsten-halogen lamp, b-wave criterion of 5 microvolts set at 400 nm and met at other wavelengths with neutral-density filters; curves are group means with SE bars and no statistical test between species is reported; all three species peaked at 525 nm with broad sensitivity 500-550 nm, the deepwater sculpin broader (475-550 nm); the abstract's full-moon depth for the sculpin (45 m) differs from the Results' figure (63 m per the page text read), a separate depth-profile result not logged here

value: physiological hearing threshold tuned to 5 kHz in both sexes
method: extracellular suction-electrode recordings from axons of auditory interneurons in the neck connective, pure sine tones 3-50 kHz; threshold curves compared between sexes
conditions: flies emerged from pupae taken from infected cicadas (Okanagana rimosa) collected in Michigan, USA, pupae held at 4 C for up to six months, males also swept from vegetation; electrophysiology N = 3 females and N = 4 males (Fig 2 caption); threshold curves of the sexes very similar in tuning and sensitivity, males relatively insensitive in the ultrasonic range; no statistical test for the threshold comparison was read; separate behavioural phonotaxis tests on 17 males (each up to three times) found males oriented to the host song but often incompletely, and scored higher for a 9 kHz song model than a 5 kHz model even though 5 kHz is the best hearing frequency; the male ear is about 8% narrower than the female ear
